serotonin regulates several genes, pathways and biological processes that affect lactation.
serotonin deficiency alters several biological processes in the mamary gland that are central for lactation.
serotonin regulates the expression of genes and pathways that are essential for mammary gland physiology and function.

the discovery of novel genes, pathways, and functions that are modulated by serotonin during lactation.
the role of serotonin in the mammary epithelium and its impact on mammary gland function during lactation.

serotonin deficiency alters the expression of numerous genes involved in mammary gland homeogenesis and lactation, and increasing peripheral serotonin in KO dams rescues some of these alterations.

serotonin regulates the expression of numerous genes in the mammary epithelial cells, which are important for lactation.

the serotonin deficiency in KO dams leads to the alteration of pathways and functions that are essential for the mammary gland homeoregulation.
